preregister.common_contract: Same fixed slots/source/grammar/per-case output budget in every arm; decoder owns all DOM and code writes. No free-translation draft or target reference.

applicability.values: Short ASCII identifier/expression-like values without whitespace or transport literals; exclude non-code original opaque spans; no source truncation.

preregister.selection_rule: On eight known development diagnostics: no structural/code/label-ownership regressions; fix at least two clear participant/predicate/condition failures versus baseline; no new clear critical semantic error on an otherwise acceptable baseline. referred to as “inner value”) is also dropped.

rows.source:
The type Arc<T> provides shared ownership of a value of type T,
allocated in the heap. Invoking clone on Arc produces
a new Arc instance, which points to the same allocation on the heap as the
source Arc, while increasing a reference count. When the last Arc
pointer to a given allocation is destroyed, the value stored in that allocation (often
referred to as “inner value”) is also dropped.

observations: All six selected paragraphs at narrow width were inspected in both arms, plus three full-page wide views. CJK glyphs are readable. No site font/CSS override was added.

No newly broken link/code formatting, displaced navigation or conspicuous paragraph-layout damage was seen in these views. Wrapped paragraph heights differ naturally. This is not a whole-site or pixel-equivalence claim.

The visually intact Python first paragraph still attributes the returned loop to RuntimeError. Rust paragraphs still reverse true/Some and true/None; these semantic failures are plainly visible in the screenshots.
Promise terminology and final fulfilled-with-value phrasing remain awkward in both arms. Semantic correctness is assessed separately from layout.
visual_review.scope: Recorded native outputs on actual public webpages through a temporary production-plumbing prototype; no model inference during these 24 replays. Four actual WASM generations are a separate File-input test.

limitations: Eight known failures are selected development diagnostics, not an accuracy sample. All already had critical baseline errors; positive non-regression controls come only from the small fresh set.
Fresh sources are new relative to the local inventory, not proven unseen in model pretraining. Three critical participant errors remain in each native arm.
The six fresh sources are now consumed confirmation data and remain evaluation-only; no training export reads them.
Manual review is by the assistant with visible arm names, not independent blinded human review.
First-visible timing is first nonempty stream content, including frame markers; it is not specifically the first Chinese word.
Native run timing is observational: lightweight decoder/postprocessing ran during portions of the development run. No native-versus-WASM speedup or statistical performance claim is made.
Model/file caches were warm; health-ready/model-ready load timings exclude first prompt prefill.
Firefox memory is sampled after launch during inference and may miss short or initial-load peaks; summed RSS double-counts shared pages, PSS is proportional.
Website replays use recorded native outputs, not live model inference, and translate selected paragraphs rather than entire sites.

The temporary prototype used a narrower bounded full-source context packet (at most 32 original opaque entries, each code value at most 96 UTF-8 bytes); oversized packets retained the old prompt. The 14 frozen eligible prompts/grammars/budgets matched exactly.
Initial progress commentary misidentified adjacent timeout prose as emphasis content; exact-slot review corrected it. No candidate was rejected for that mistaken scope claim.
Official Microsoft/Google credentials and new GPU training were outside this experiment.
